speaker: Doctor
text: To understand the nature of your unresponsiveness, can you describe if anyone witnesses these episodes and what specific movements or sounds occur? Did you experience any loss of consciousness or confusion afterward?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for those details; the "muddy taste" is a specific clue we need to investigate. Have you noticed any specific triggers like flashing lights, strong smells, or particular emotional states before these spells start? Also, does he have any known allergies or a history of seizures?

REQUEST TEST: EEG

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The EEG results showing right temporal lobe spikes are highly suggestive of focal epilepsy. Can you describe if the hand gestures he made during the episode were rhythmic (like automatisms) or purposeful? Additionally, does he have any history of head trauma or encephalitis, and has he experienced any febrile seizures in the past?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Temporal Lobe Epilepsy. The combination of focal automatisms (hand gestures), ictal oral automatisms (muddy taste), post-ictal confusion, and right temporal spikes confirms this diagnosis. No further tests are required at this time.
